intro.title: What does Exyconn build for events and entertainment?
intro.definition: is a set of agents that sells and registers, answers attendee questions, sends promotions, chases vendors and runs check-in, so a small event team can handle a crowd many times its size. Exyconn designs, builds and runs these agents on your ticketing or registration platform, your CRM, your payment gateway and your WhatsApp Business account. Your producers keep the creative and the decisions; the agents keep up with the messages.

benefits.title: Why organisers are doing this now

items.text: Questions spike in the hours around an on-sale and on show day. Hiring for those peaks is expensive; leaving them unanswered costs tickets.
Attendees expect tickets, directions and schedule changes on WhatsApp, not buried in an email.
Paid reach is costly. Following up warm leads from past events is cheaper than finding new ones.
One late vendor or a missed sound check can push a whole run-of-show. Someone has to chase every confirmation.
Sponsors want proof of footfall and engagement soon after the event, not three weeks later.

demo.title: whatsapp · festival help desk
demo.caption: An attendee asks about re-entry and parking on show day; the agent answers from the event policy and resends her pass.

messages.text: Hey, if I leave the venue for dinner can I come back in?
Hi Priyanka! Re-entry is allowed until 8pm. Keep your wristband on and scan your pass again at Gate 2 when you return.
Ok. Also is there parking? And I can't find my ticket email
Paid parking is at the P3 lot, a five-minute walk from Gate 2. I've resent your QR pass here, it's 2 × General Admission for Saturday.
Enjoy the show! The headliner is on at 9:15pm, and I'll message you if the timing changes.

props.label: The reality
props.title: Where an event team's hours actually go
props.lede: Every producer has the same list. Most of it happens in the fortnight before the event and all of it at once.

items.title: The same questions, thousands of times
items.text: Age limits, bag policy, set times, where's my ticket. They arrive on Instagram, WhatsApp, email and the ticketing platform's inbox, all in the same week.

items.title: Registrations that don't line up
items.text: Delegate lists come from a form, a ticketing platform and a sponsor's spreadsheet. Duplicates, missing company names and unpaid passes are cleaned up by hand.

items.title: Promotion that stops at the first post
items.text: Early-bird deadlines, lineup announcements and reminders to past buyers need a steady rhythm, but the team is busy booking acts and venues.

items.title: Vendors chased on personal phones
items.text: Sound, light, staging, catering, security and decor each have load-in times and dependencies. Confirmations live in dozens of WhatsApp chats.

items.title: Queues at the gate
items.text: Scanners fail, guest lists are on paper and on-spot registrations slow everyone down. The first impression of the event is a long line.

items.title: Reports assembled weeks later
items.text: Sales by channel, actual attendance, session turnout and feedback sit in separate tools, so the sponsor report and the debrief come late.

offerings.title: Six jobs AI takes off your team's plate

items.title: Ticketing and registration
items.text: Takes registrations and ticket purchases in chat with a payment link, issues the pass from your ticketing platform, and handles transfers and name changes within your rules. Refund requests go to a person.

items.title: Attendee questions, before and on the day
items.text: Answers on WhatsApp, Instagram and web chat from your FAQ, schedule and venue map in the attendee's language, and resends passes on request. Complaints and safety issues go straight to the ops team.

items.title: Promotion and campaigns
items.text: Sends opted-in past attendees early-bird reminders, lineup news and last-call messages through your CRM, and drafts social posts for your team to approve.

items.title: Vendor and run-of-show coordination
items.text: Confirms load-in slots, deliverables and contacts with every vendor from the production schedule, nudges anyone who hasn't confirmed and alerts the producer when a dependency slips.

items.title: Check-in and access
items.text: Sends QR passes before the day, checks scans against the attendee list by ticket type or zone, prints badges for walk-ins and gives the gate team a live count.

items.title: Post-event reports
items.text: Combines ticket sales by channel, check-ins, session attendance and feedback survey answers into a debrief and a sponsor report, ready the morning after.

props.label: A day with it running
props.title: One day before a two-day business conference
props.lede: Follow the last full day before the doors open. Each moment lights the part of the event the agent is working on.

moments.title: Vendors confirm their load-in
moments.text: The AV, staging and catering teams each get their load-in slot for tonight. Two confirm; the florist hasn't replied, so the producer is told before 8am.

moments.title: Last-call message to past delegates
moments.text: Opted-in delegates from last year who haven't registered get a short note with tomorrow's keynote speakers and a registration link.

moments.title: A late team registration
moments.text: A company registers five delegates through the chat. The agent collects names and GSTIN for the invoice, sends the payment link and issues five passes once it is paid.

moments.title: Questions about parking and the agenda
moments.text: Two hundred messages arrive after the final reminder: parking, dress code, the workshop room. The agent answers them; a delegate needing wheelchair access is passed to the venue lead.

moments.title: The gate is ready for tomorrow
moments.text: Every registered delegate has a QR pass on WhatsApp, the scanner list is synced and badges for VIPs and speakers are queued to print.

moments.title: The pre-event numbers
moments.text: Registrations by ticket type and source, expected turnout per session and open vendor items go to the organising team as one summary.

items.question: Does this replace our event staff or volunteers?
items.answer: No. It takes the repeated questions, confirmations and reminders so your team can run the floor. Refunds, complaints, accessibility needs and safety issues are always passed to a person, with the conversation attached.

items.question: Can it work with the ticketing platform we already use?
items.answer: Usually, yes. Most ticketing and registration platforms offer an API, webhooks or attendee exports, and we connect to whichever your platform supports. In the first week we confirm what we can read, such as orders and passes, and what we can write back.

items.question: What if the event changes at the last minute?
items.answer: Your team updates the schedule or FAQ in one place and the agent answers from the new version straight away. For anything urgent, such as a gate change or a delayed set, a producer approves the message and it is sent to affected ticket holders.

items.question: How is attendee data protected?
items.answer: Attendee data stays in your systems and an environment set up for your events, with role-based access and a log of every message. Promotions go only to people who opted in, and the setup follows the privacy law that applies, such as India's DPDP Act 2023 or the GDPR.

items.question: Can attendees message in their own language?
items.answer: Yes. The agent replies in the language the attendee writes in, including Hindi and other Indian languages. Your FAQ and policies are written once and answered the same way in every language.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on attendee numbers, channels and how many events you run a year. Some organisers start with a help desk for one event; others set it up across a season. Tell us about your calendar and we'll send a fixed quote.
